rationale: Exempt only /docs and /search, where q is HTML-escaped; this also addresses the documented benign CRS false positives on those routes. Keep CRS inspection and anomaly scoring on all other routes, adding narrowly scoped signatures for SQL tautologies/UNION SELECT, script tags or trace-triggering event handlers, and traversal paths to secret.txt. Dev observations show these attack families were blocked, while benign traversal to public/readme.txt was a false positive; the file signature avoids blocking that observed path.
risks: No test data is available, and dev evidence is limited: crafted SQL/XSS/file variants may evade these signatures, while broader CRS rules can still block benign q values on attack routes. The file pattern targets the disclosed secret path rather than general traversal, so other sensitive-file paths are not covered by this added rule.
